newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end up as flagging gold rallies.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end up as flagging gold rallies.

text.p: South African gold shares on Thursday basked in the warmth of a much-needed rally as a bullion price firming to around $320 an ounce gave a shot in the arm to the ailing sector, dealers said.
Gold also got support from the start of the second quarter reporting season as Goldfields of South Africa Ltd came in with results that were not as bad as had been feared.
The gold index jumped 42.1 points, or 4.65 percent, to 947.4 as Goldfields put on 200 cents to 95.00 rand after posting a drop in net pre-capex profit from 236.42 million rand to 192.3 million rand.
However, dealers warned that the index was not out of trouble yet, though signs of institutional buying were creeping back into the sector from investors with a longer-term view on its prospects.
The positive sentiment spilled from golds into the rest of the market and the all-share index added 38.7 points to 7,337.9 as the industrials index gained 39.2 points to 8,798.5.
The market also got a boost from a steadier rand and local bond market and PPI data that confirmed inflation is on a downwards trend.
The day was busy with shares worth 920 million rands changing hands, though values were hugely boosted by a series of massive deals by broker ING Barings in furniture firm Ellerine Holdings Ltd.
They included a foreign purchase of 2.8 million shares, a bookover of 2.0 million shares and an asset swap of 1.6 million shares. Ellerine stock lost 75 cents to end at 35.25 rand.
